source: REF·DB v1 standards register, regrouped, with the standards the rebuilt pages cite. Energetic-material and initiation standards are outside the site scope.

standards.title: Technical product documentation & specification: the UK umbrella drawing standard
standards.why: Put it in every title block. It invokes the ISO GPS suite below, so "to BS 8888" pulls in datums, fits, surface texture etc. by reference.

standards.title: Dimensioning & tolerancing (US)
standards.why: US-origin defence programmes and primes. Differs from ISO in defaults: see the GD&T page (Rule #1 vs independency).

standards.title: Presentation: line types, views, sections, hatching
standards.why: When you argue about hidden detail, section conventions or line weights.

standards.title: Drawing sheet sizes & frames / title block data fields
standards.why: Setting up templates; what must appear in a title block.

standards.title: Presentation of dimensions and tolerances
standards.why: How to arrange dimensions, leaders, chain vs baseline.

standards.title: Lettering on technical drawings
standards.why: Template/font arguments, min text heights for microfilm/scan legibility.

standards.title: Edge condition callout (burr / undercut / passing)
standards.why: Deburr requirements: the ⌐ edge symbol with +/- values instead of a vague "break all edges" note.

standards.title: Welding symbols
standards.why: Any welded fabrication: fillet/butt symbols, arrow vs other side, site welds, weld-all-round.

standards.title: GPS fundamentals: the independency principle
standards.why: The ISO ground rule: size does NOT control form unless you add Ⓔ. Explains half of all ISO/ASME arguments.

standards.title: Geometrical tolerancing: symbols, zones, definitions
standards.why: The core GD&T document in the ISO world. Zone definitions for all characteristics.

standards.title: Datums and datum systems
standards.why: How datum features become datums; targets, common datums A-B, simulators.

standards.title: MMR / LMR: Ⓜ Ⓛ modifiers & bonus tolerance
standards.why: Functional gauging, clearance-hole patterns, when bonus tolerance applies.

standards.title: Pattern specification / combined zones (CZ, SIM)
standards.why: Tolerancing hole patterns as a group in ISO syntax.

standards.title: Limits & fits: IT grades and the H7/g6 system
standards.why: Every fit callout. Tables of numeric limits per size band.

standards.title: General tolerances (linear/angular + geometry), e.g. "ISO 2768-mK"
standards.why: Legacy but still everywhere. Part 2 is withdrawn in favour of ISO 22081: don't mix regimes on one drawing.

standards.title: General specified geometrical & size tolerances
standards.why: The modern replacement for blanket drawing tolerances under BS 8888.

standards.title: Surface texture: symbols, parameters (Ra, Rz), rules
standards.why: Current surface-finish callout rules (replaces ISO 1302/4287: old drawings still cite those).

standards.title: Non-rigid parts
standards.why: Thin sheet/flexible parts: the "free state" vs restrained condition note, F modifier.

standards.title: Screw threads: representation & callout
standards.why: How M6×1-6H, thread depth and section conventions are drawn.

standards.title: Hex head bolts (part thread / full thread)
standards.why: Standard metric hex bolts for BOMs.

standards.title: Hexagon socket head cap screws
standards.why: The default cap-head. Counterbore data derives from it.

standards.title: Hex nuts / plain washers
standards.why: Completing the joint on the BOM.

standards.title: Dowel pins (soft / hardened, m6)
standards.why: Location pins; pair with reamed H7 holes.

standards.title: Socket set screws (flat, cone, dog, cup point)
standards.why: Grub screws: pick the point style deliberately.

standards.title: O-rings: metric sizes, tolerances, quality (incl. AS568 cross-refs)
standards.why: Primary o-ring size + quality reference; part 2 covers housing design.

standards.title: O-rings: imperial (BS 1806) & UK metric (BS 4518): legacy
standards.why: Heritage UK drawings; BS 4518 grooves differ from ISO 3601: don't mix.

standards.title: US o-ring dash sizes (-0XX, -1XX…)
standards.why: US-designed equipment; "-214" style callouts.

standards.title: US aerospace standard hardware series
standards.why: Flight fasteners: e.g. NAS bolts, MS21042 self-locking nuts, AN washers. Procurement by exact part number.

standards.title: Aerospace material specs, e.g. AMS 4911 (Ti-6Al-4V sheet), AMS 5643 (17-4PH bar)
standards.why: Procuring flight material with pedigree; the number to put in the material block.

standards.title: Metallic material design allowables (ex MIL-HDBK-5)
standards.why: A/B-basis strength values the stress office will insist on.

standards.title: Aluminium: designations, extrusion & sheet/plate conditions
standards.why: Calling up commercial aluminium correctly (e.g. EN AW-6082-T6 to BS EN 755-2).

standards.title: Legacy UK aerospace aluminium/steel specs, e.g. L168 (2014A-T6511 bar)
standards.why: Heritage drawings and MoD legacy fleets still call these; keep the cross-ref table handy.

standards.title: Tensile testing of metals
standards.why: When cert values are queried: how UTS/proof are derived.

standards.title: Design & airworthiness requirements for service aircraft (UK MoD)
standards.why: The design bible on UK military air programmes: structure, systems, factors.

standards.title: Quality assurance procedural requirements
standards.why: MoD contract QA requirements incl. deliverable records.

standards.title: Protective treatments of metals (individual parts for anodising, plating, painting…)
standards.why: Calling up finishes on MoD work; each treatment has its own part number: cite the exact one.

standards.title: Aerospace quality management system
standards.why: Why every change needs a paper trail; supplier approval questions.

standards.title: First Article Inspection (FAIR)
standards.why: Ballooned drawings & the forms the inspector fills for a first-off.

standards.title: Aero engine supply-chain quality (RM13xxx series)
standards.why: Engine-sector customers (e.g. R-R supply chain): PPAP-style deliverables.

standards.title: Certification specs: large / normal category aeroplanes
standards.why: Civil airworthiness context; what "certifiable" means for your design.

standards.title: Environmental test methods (shock, vibe, temp, humidity…)
standards.why: Defence equipment qual test levels: design for the test.

standards.title: Item identification / part marking (US)
standards.why: How US programmes want parts marked; pair with your customer's marking spec.

standards.title: MOD safety & environmental management of Ordnance, Munitions and Explosives (OME)
standards.why: The UK MoD governance framework for anything explosive-related, across the whole Manufacture-to-Target-or-Disposal sequence. Sets the safety case, review panel and clearance expectations your hardware sits inside. Note the published parts are being replaced: always confirm the current issue with your safety authority.

standards.title: Design requirements for weapons and associated systems
standards.why: Mandatory design requirements (Part 1), supplementary/design-process requirements (Part 2) and safety-and-suitability-for-service test procedures (Part 4). Limited distribution: get it via your Design Authority, not the open web.

standards.title: Proof of ordnance, munitions, armour and explosives
standards.why: Part 1 requirements / Part 2 guidance. The generic proof policy applying to weapons, munitions and explosive-related components: what proof firing and testing your hardware must survive.

standards.title: Environmental handbook for defence materiel
standards.why: UK equivalent of MIL-STD-810: the environmental conditions and test methods (vibration, shock, temperature, humidity, transit) your motor hardware must be qualified against.

standards.title: Safety management requirements for defence systems (incl. safety-related software)
standards.why: Hazard analysis, safety case structure and evidence expectations. 00-056 is the general system safety standard your programme safety case follows.

standards.title: Insensitive Munitions (IM) policy and assessment
standards.why: NATO IM policy: the six IM threat tests (fast/slow cook-off, bullet impact, fragment impact, sympathetic reaction, shaped charge jet). IM response drives real hardware decisions: case venting features, liner and insulation choice. AOP-39 holds the response descriptors (Type I to VI) and the recognised design techniques.

standards.title: Boiler & pressure vessel code
standards.why: Used for ground pressure equipment, test rigs, gas storage and pressurisation hardware. Flight motor cases are normally designed to programme-specific criteria rather than BPVC: check which regime applies before you start.

standards.title: Space systems: metallic pressure vessels & COPVs
standards.why: The recognised design, analysis and test criteria for metallic pressure vessels and composite overwrapped pressure vessels: damage tolerance, proof factors, leak-before-burst logic.

standards.title: Space systems: pressure vessels and pressurised structures
standards.why: International equivalent for pressure vessel design and qualification requirements on space hardware.

standards.title: Fracture control requirements & NDE
standards.why: The fracture-control framework: which parts are fracture-critical, what flaw sizes you must assume, and what NDE sensitivity is required to find them. Excellent reference even on non-NASA work.

standards.title: Pyrometry: furnace and heat treat control
standards.why: Heat treat is a special process: this governs furnace surveys, thermocouple classes and instrumentation. Call it up whenever heat treatment is a controlled characteristic.

standards.title: Heat treat, NDT, welding, chemical processing, coatings
standards.why: Not a design standard: the accreditation your suppliers need for special processes. If a process can"t be verified by inspecting the finished part, it"s a special process and needs an approved source.

standards.title: Fluorescent penetrant inspection
standards.why: The everyday NDT callout for surface flaw detection on machined and welded parts. State the penetrant sensitivity level on the drawing.

standards.title: Magnetic particle & radiographic inspection
standards.why: MPI for ferromagnetic parts (case steels), RT for welds and castings. Specify acceptance class, not just "inspect".

standards.title: Ultrasonic inspection of wrought products
standards.why: Billet and forging quality classes (e.g. AA/A/B): how you demand clean material for a fracture-critical case or closure.

standards.title: Aluminium: chemical composition of wrought products
standards.why: Defines EN AW-6082 etc. Pair with the product standard for properties: composition alone is not a specification.

standards.title: Aluminium: mechanical properties: sheet & plate / extrusion / drawn bar & tube
standards.why: The properties half of an aluminium call-out. Values depend on product form and thickness: quote the right one.

standards.title: Aluminium castings: composition and mechanical properties
standards.why: Replaces BS 1490 LM designations for new work.

standards.title: Hot rolled structural steels
standards.why: S355 and friends. Rigs, stands, handling equipment.

standards.title: Quenched and tempered alloy steels
standards.why: 25CrMo4, 42CrMo4, 34CrNiMo6: the EN equivalents of 4130/4140/4340.

standards.title: Steel designation systems: names and numbers
standards.why: How to read 34CrNiMo6 and 1.6582. Worth ten minutes of your life.

standards.title: Stainless steels: sheet & plate / bar and sections
standards.why: The correct UK call-out for 304L, 316L, 321, 17-4PH and friends.

standards.title: Types of inspection document (2.1, 2.2, 3.1, 3.2)
standards.why: Which certificate you get. 3.1 is the usual minimum for anything structural; 3.2 adds independent verification.

standards.title: Steels & alloys for fasteners and creep-resisting service
standards.why: A286, superalloy bar and hot bolting material in the EN system.

standards.title: Tool steels
standards.why: H13, D2, O1 equivalents for tooling and moulds.

standards.title: Grey and spheroidal graphite cast irons
standards.why: Machine bases, housings, damping-critical tooling.

standards.title: Copper and copper alloys: rod, free-machining rod, and conductors
standards.why: CW614N brass, CuBe2, Cu-ETP: the EN copper designations.

standards.title: Magnesium alloy castings: designation and properties
standards.why: EN-MC magnesium designations; pair with the process approval for aerospace work.

standards.title: Metallic materials: tensile testing at room temperature
standards.why: How UTS and proof stress on your cert were actually derived.

standards.title: Vickers and Rockwell hardness tests
standards.why: Specifying and interpreting a hardness requirement correctly.

standards.title: Charpy pendulum impact test
standards.why: Toughness requirements on case and structural steels.

standards.title: Non-destructive testing: penetrant testing
standards.why: The correct UK reference for FPI. State the sensitivity level and acceptance.

standards.title: Non-destructive testing: magnetic particle testing
standards.why: Ferromagnetic parts only; the EN equivalent of ASTM E1444.

standards.title: NDT of welds: radiographic testing
standards.why: Weld RT technique and image quality requirements.

standards.title: Non-destructive testing: ultrasonic testing
standards.why: UT general principles and sensitivity setting.

standards.title: NDT: qualification and certification of personnel
standards.why: Who is allowed to sign off your inspection, and to what level.

standards.title: Welding procedure specification and qualification
standards.why: WPS/WPQR: what makes a weld procedure legitimate.

standards.title: Weld quality levels for steel / aluminium
standards.why: Quality level B, C or D. This is where welded fabrication cost lives.

standards.title: Qualification testing of welders and operators
standards.why: Welder approval to match your procedure.

standards.title: Hot dip galvanizing / electroplated zinc coatings
standards.why: Coating thickness classes for ground equipment and structures.

standards.title: Fasteners: electroplated coating systems
standards.why: Fastener plating, including the hydrogen embrittlement relief requirement.

standards.title: Mechanical properties of fasteners: steel / stainless
standards.why: Where property classes 8.8, 10.9, 12.9 and A2-70, A4-80 are actually defined.

standards.title: Fast heating (fast cook-off) test procedures
standards.why: Liquid fuel fire engulfment. Required response no worse than Type V (burning).

standards.title: Slow heating (slow cook-off) test procedures
standards.why: The hardest thermal case: the whole item heats together, so the case is still strong when the propellant reacts.

standards.title: Bullet impact test procedures
standards.why: Small-arms strike. Venting area and case fragmentation behaviour drive the result.

standards.title: Fragment impact test procedures
standards.why: Standard conical-nosed steel fragment at high velocity: a far more energetic stimulus than a bullet.

standards.title: Sympathetic reaction test procedures
standards.why: Donor/acceptor in stowage configuration. Packaging and spacing count toward the outcome. Type III or better.

standards.title: Shaped charge jet impact test procedures
standards.why: Hard to mitigate by case design alone; relaxed to Type III or better.

standards.title: Metric screw threads: general plan and tolerances
standards.why: The series (which pitches exist) and the tolerance system (what 6H/6g means). The pair behind every metric thread callout.

standards.title: Unified inch threads / UNJ controlled-root aerospace threads
standards.why: B1.1 defines UNC/UNF and classes 1-3; AS8879 is the fatigue-rated UNJ form for aerospace externals.

standards.title: Pipe threads: parallel (G) not pressure-tight / taper (R) pressure-tight
standards.why: The two BSP families. G seals on a face, R seals on the thread: mixing the logic is why fittings weep.

standards.title: Whitworth (BSW/BSF) and BA threads
standards.why: Obsolescent: retained for legacy repair and heritage support only. Never for new design.

standards.title: General tolerances: linear and angular dimensions
standards.why: Classes f/m/c/v. The tolerance that applies to every dimension you did not tolerance individually.

standards.title: General geometrical tolerances for features without individual indication
standards.why: Classes H/K/L for straightness, flatness, perpendicularity, symmetry and runout. Superseded by ISO 22081 but still widely used.

standards.title: General geometrical specification and general size specification
standards.why: The modern replacement for ISO 2768-2: a general geometrical specification referenced to stated datums rather than fixed H/K/L classes.

standards.title: Geometrical product specifications: limits and fits
standards.why: The ISO fit system in full, with the numeric tables.

standards.title: Dimensional tolerancing: linear sizes
standards.why: Modern size specification modifiers, including the envelope requirement Ⓔ.

standards.title: Geometrical tolerancing, datums, and MMR/LMR
standards.why: The GPS core set, all adopted as BS EN ISO in the UK.

standards.title: GPS for moulded parts: dimensional and geometrical tolerances
standards.why: Casting tolerance grades (DCTG): how to tolerance an as-cast surface sensibly.

standards.title: Aerospace MJ threads: general requirements and limits of size
standards.why: MJ bolts and nuts with the controlled root radius (0.15011P to 0.18042P), 4h6h external and 4H5H internal. An MJ bolt goes into an MJ nut or insert, not a standard M thread.

standards.title: NPT taper pipe threads (inch)
standards.why: US ports and fittings that seal on the thread with a sealant. Not interchangeable with BSPT (55°) or with G.

standards.title: Straight-thread ports with an O-ring seal (inch / metric)
standards.why: Ports that seal on an O-ring in a spot face, not on the thread: the preferred port on flight hardware. Pairs with the AS568 900-series rings.

standards.title: Ports and stud ends with ISO 228-1 (G) threads
standards.why: How a parallel G port seals: an elastomer seal, a bonded seal or a metal-to-metal face. A G thread itself never seals.

standards.title: Helical-coil inserts / key-locked inserts
standards.why: Inserts for tapped holes in soft parent material. Rate them by their specification, not by a stripping calculation, and prime stainless inserts in aluminium.

standards.title: Counterbore diameters for cap screws
standards.why: The counterbore for a socket-head cap screw (ISO 4762): ⌀18 for M10, ⌀11 for M6. Sets the head clearance and the bolt pitch.

standards.title: Hand torque tools: design conformance and calibration
standards.why: The torque wrench tolerance is part of the preload scatter. Calibrated tools on the build instruction, not "a torque wrench".

standards.title: Threaded fastening systems for spaceflight hardware
standards.why: Preload uncertainty, separation and fastener margins, thread engagement, locking features and procured nuts and inserts. A clear method even on non-NASA work.

standards.title: Systematic calculation of highly stressed bolted joints
standards.why: The full bolted-joint method: stiffness, load introduction, embedding, tightening factor, eccentric loads and the minimum engagement length.

standards.title: Structural design and test factors of safety for spaceflight hardware
standards.why: Design and test factors for metallic and composite structure and the proof-test logic. Programme factors override it; it explains where they come from.

standards.title: Space engineering: structures (-01 fracture control, -02 pressurised hardware, -10 factors of safety)
standards.why: The European space structures standards: the pressure vessel and pressurised hardware rules, fracture control and the factors of safety.

standards.title: Composite Materials Handbook
standards.why: Composite allowables and their statistical basis, test methods and design guidance: the composite counterpart of MMPDS.

standards.title: Fracture toughness testing (KIc, J-integral)
standards.why: How a toughness value was measured: plane-strain validity, specimen size and orientation. Check them before you use a KIc in a crack calculation.

standards.title: Density of plastics by displacement
standards.why: Measured density of mouldings and composites where the mass matters: real parts have voids that a calculated density does not.

standards.title: Durometer (Shore) hardness of rubber and plastics
standards.why: Shore A and D hardness of seals, pottings and elastomer parts: state the scale and the test conditions.

standards.title: Outgassing of materials in a vacuum (TML, CVCM)
standards.why: Screening of polymers, adhesives and pottings for vacuum use: total mass loss 1.0% and collected condensables 0.10% are the usual limits. Use data for the actual product and cure.

standards.title: Hydrogen embrittlement: pre- and post-treatment of plated steel
standards.why: The relief bake for steels above about 1000 MPa after plating or pickling, with the time limit to start it.

standards.title: Heat treatment of steel parts
standards.why: Hardening, tempering and stress relief of steel parts, with the furnace and atmosphere controls (pyrometry to AMS 2750).

standards.title: Heat treatment of wrought aluminium alloy parts
standards.why: Solution treatment, quench and ageing of aluminium parts: how a T6 or T73 condition is made and checked.

standards.title: Passivation of stainless steel
standards.why: Removes free iron after machining so that the oxide film forms. Call it up for every machined stainless part.

standards.title: Anodic coatings for aluminium (Type I, II, III)
standards.why: Chromic, sulphuric and hard anodising: state the type, the class (dyed or not) and the thickness, and mask the features that must stay bare.

standards.title: Revision of engineering drawings and associated documents
standards.why: Revision letters (no I, O, Q, S, X or Z; AA after Y), the revision table and what a revision must record.

standards.title: Digital product definition data practices (model-based definition)
standards.why: When the model is the master: annotation in the model, and how a drawing-less release is controlled.

standards.title: Engineering drawing practices
standards.why: US drawing types, parts lists and the documentation rules around the drawing.

standards.title: Decision rules for proving conformity or non-conformity with specifications
standards.why: How measurement uncertainty is used to accept or reject a part: the inspector must state the decision rule, and guard bands come from it.

standards.title: Configuration management
standards.why: Identification, change control, status accounting and audits. The change classes (major/minor, Class I/II) and the change board come from here.

standards.title: Electronic documents for long-term preservation
standards.why: The archive format for released drawings and reports: fonts and images embedded, no dependence on outside software.

standards.title: Managed model-based 3D engineering
standards.why: The neutral 3D format that carries PMI (tolerances and annotation) for the archive and for model-based definition.

standards.title: Long-term archiving and retrieval of digital product data
standards.why: Aerospace practice for keeping 3D data readable for the life of the product plus its retention period.

standards.title: Human factors for designers of systems
standards.why: Reach, force, posture and access for maintenance: the UK source for the human-factors limits of a task.

standards.title: Human engineering
standards.why: The US human-factors design criteria: hand forces, access openings and tool clearances.

standards.title: Wiring, aerospace vehicle
standards.why: Harness routing, clamping, bend radius and separation. Reserve the space for the harness, not a thin line.

standards.title: Cleanliness levels and cleaning methods for oxygen-enriched environments
standards.why: Cleaning LOX and oxygen hardware to a stated particle and non-volatile residue level before assembly. Write the level on the drawing.

standards.title: Evaluating metals for oxygen service
standards.why: Ranks metals by their ignition and burn resistance in oxygen: why Monel and copper alloys go where the flow impinges, and titanium nowhere.

standards.title: Evaluating nonmetallic materials for oxygen service
standards.why: Seats, seals and lubricants for oxygen: PTFE, PCTFE and fluorinated greases, and the tests that clear them.

standards.title: Ignition sensitivity to mechanical impact in liquid and gaseous oxygen
standards.why: The LOX impact test that a polymer, a lubricant or a composite must pass before it touches LOX.

standards.title: Autogenous ignition temperature in high-pressure oxygen
standards.why: The temperature at which a polymer or a lubricant ignites in oxygen without a spark: one input to an oxygen compatibility assessment.

standards.title: Flammability, offgassing and compatibility requirements and test procedures
standards.why: NASA's material tests for flammability and oxygen compatibility, including mechanical impact in LOX (Test 13A).

standards.title: Guide to safety of hydrogen and hydrogen systems (ANSI/AIAA)
standards.why: Design, materials and operation of gaseous and liquid hydrogen systems: embrittlement, leaks, venting and the cold.

standards.title: Hydrogen piping and pipelines
standards.why: Material and strength limits for hydrogen piping, including which steels may be used and at what strength.

standards.title: Cylindrical helical springs: compression springs, calculation and design
standards.why: Rate, stress with the stress correction factor, solid length, the minimum gaps between coils and buckling for a compression spring; and the permissible stress from the wire strength.

standards.title: Cylindrical helical springs made from round wire: quality specifications
standards.why: The tolerance grades (1, 2, 3) for coil diameter, free length, load and the squareness of a spring. Name the grade on the drawing.

standards.title: Steel wire for mechanical springs: patented, oil-hardened and tempered, stainless
standards.why: The spring wire grades and their minimum tensile strength by diameter, which sets the permissible stress of the spring.
